intervals.quote: The construction of the 100 liters detector has been approved and funded by INFN starting from 2004

intervals.label: construction and assembly of the 100-litre detector
intervals.note: Start: review of 2013 ('started in 2005'). End: 'assembled in 2008 at LNGS' (A. Zani, 2014 repository abstract); the review says the detector 'had been commissioned' by 2009.
intervals.quote: Construction of the 100-liter detector started in 2005 and by 2009 the detector had been commissioned at LNGS

intervals.label: commissioning and technical runs of the 100-litre detector
intervals.note: The collaboration site's news item '07/05/09: Started 100 liter filling procedure' (date format ambiguous, read as 2009); the review says problems with high-voltage delivery and with the stability of the wavelength-shifting layers halted the first technical run, a second test in 2010 still had high-voltage problems; a technical run was taken in 2011 (Zani 2014).
intervals.quote: a second test was conducted in 2010, but high voltage problems persisted. No update on WARP140 has been reported recently.

intervals.label: 2.3-litre prototype WIMP-search data
intervals.note: The prototype had been installed at LNGS by November 2004 (arXiv:astro-ph/0411491) and the first physics results (96.5 kg d exposure, 52.76 days live) were published in 2007-2008.
intervals.quote: from the 2.3-liter prototype were acquired in 2005

intervals.label: 100-litre technical runs
intervals.note: No physics run was ever taken (Zani 2014).

intervals.label: completed (no physics run; programme ended without further reports)
intervals.note: 2011 is the year of the last documented activity (a technical run); no end-of-programme statement or decommissioning date was found. The review of 2013 says no update on the 100-litre detector had been reported.
intervals.quote: Though it never actually performed a physics run, a technical run was taken in 2011, to characterise the detector response.

target_mass.quote: a 100-liter detector built from low background components and using 140 kg of isotopically purified argon

summary.plain: WArP (WIMP Argon Programme) was a Gran Sasso programme that pioneered two-phase liquid argon detectors for WIMP dark matter. Its 2.3-litre prototype gave the first physics results; a 100-litre detector was assembled in 2008 and tested until about 2011 but never completed a physics run.
summary.technical: Two-phase (liquid and gas) argon detector reading both scintillation (S1) and ionisation through electroluminescence (S2) with PMTs, using the S2/S1 ratio and the pulse shape to reject electron recoils. Prototype: 2.3 l chamber (1.87 l sensitive volume), 96.5 kg d, first physics results published 2007-2008 (a 2013 review quotes a WIMP-nucleon limit of 1e-42 cm^2). Main detector: WARP140, 100 l target (140 kg of argon, 37 PMTs) inside an 8 t liquid-argon active veto in a double-walled cryostat; assembled in 2008, high-voltage and wavelength-shifter problems halted its technical runs in 2009-2010, a technical run was taken in 2011; no physics run.

technology.quote: WARP is a double phase argon detector for dark matter survey
